text: IN THE NEWSOctober 12, 2026Housing, Iran, and Public Lands Divide 4th Congressional District CandidatesUtah Public RadioUPR's recap of the Snow College debate. Larsen, a Marine combat veteran, argues that ending the Iran War would bring the quickest relief at the pump and that Kennedy gave up Congress's Article I power to declare war. He says ending "egregious tariffs" would make homes more affordable to build, and that public lands must remain in public hands to protect the ecosystem and water supplies.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 12, 2026Utah Congressional District 4: U.S. Rep. Mike Kennedy Faces 3 ChallengersThe Salt Lake TribuneThe Tribune's voter guide to the 4th District race, with each candidate answering the same questions. Larsen, a Marine Corps combat veteran and self-described "Blue Dog Democrat," backs the Unrig Washington campaign to ban congressional stock trading, reject corporate PAC money and end dark money; ties the affordability crisis to the Iran War and its cost; calls for federal help converting farm irrigation to put water back into the Great Salt Lake; and says Congress should "agree better" on the 90% of issues voters share.Read More→

IN THE NEWSOctober 15, 2026Utah Congressional District 4 (“CD4”): Burt, Kennedy, Larsen, and WrightNetwork of Utah ModeratesThe Network of Utah Moderates' guide to the 4th District race. It says Larsen, a Marine veteran who grew up in a trailer park and spent time in foster care, would bring a "highly unusual and, in our opinion, helpful background to Congress," notes he is one of the few candidates talking about helping both farmers and veterans, and credits him for not criticizing voters across the aisle. The group says it cannot in good conscience recommend Kennedy, and that Larsen has more momentum and a better chance of making a dent.Read More→
